title: Attio MCP
snippet:
Attio MCP is Attio’s hosted MCP server that gives AI tools secure access to your Attio workspace. It’s designed to work seamlessly with popular AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and more.
### Why use Attio MCP?
- **Easy setup** — Connect through simple OAuth with one-click installation for supported AI tools
- **Natural language CRM management** — Manage your entire Attio workspace through conversational AI instead of clicking through multiple screens
- **Full workspace access** — AI tools can search, read, create, and update records across your CRM—people, companies, deals, tasks, and notes
- **Optimized for AI** — Built specifically for AI agents with efficient data formatting and human-readable responses
- **Secure by design** — Authenticates as your Attio user with OAuth, and read operations are auto-approved while write operations request confirmation

### Prerequisites
Before connecting Attio MCP, ensure you have:
1. An active Attio workspace
2. An MCP-compatible AI client (Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc.)
### Connecting to Attio MCP
Attio MCP uses OAuth authentication, so you simply log in with your Attio account—no API keys required.
#### Add as a Custom Connector
In your AI tool of choice, add the following URL as a custom MCP connector:
```
https://mcp.attio.com/mcp
```
**For Claude Desktop or Claude.ai:**
1. Open Settings -> Connectors -> Browse connectors
2. Search for Attio
3. Install Attio
**For ChatGPT:**
1. Open Apps
2. Search for Attio
3. Connect Attio
**For other MCP clients:** Add `https://mcp.attio.com/mcp` as a remote MCP server and complete the OAuth authentication when prompted. Once connected, you’ll be authenticated as your Attio user with access to your workspace data.

Attio MCP applies per-workspace rate limits to tool calls. Tools are grouped into tiers, and each tier has its own limit. Tools in the same tier share a single bucket per workspace, so calls to any tool in a tier count against the same limit.

> Attio's MCP server connects your CRM to the AI tools your team already has open. Sign in once from ChatGPT, Claude, Notion, or anything else that speaks MCP, then search records, log notes, create tasks, and update deals without switching tabs. Your AI tools can read from Attio and write back to it, over Universal Context — the deepest context layer in agentic CRM — with access scoped to each person and actions verified before they run.
## What is Attio's MCP server?
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for connecting AI tools to the systems they need. Attio's MCP server makes your workspace available to any MCP client, so the tool you already have open can read from Attio and write back to it.
It combines three things:
- **Speaks your language.** No views to build, no filters to set. Get insights and take action in conversation.
- **Full workspace access.** Search, create, and update across your CRM records and activities.
- **Secure by design.** Authenticate via OAuth with user-scoped permissions.
The result: your CRM stops being a place you always have to go and becomes something your AI tools can always reach, in every tool your team already works in.

- **471K+** — average MCP calls made from Attio workspaces every day
- **40%** — of Enterprise workspaces use Attio MCP
## Core Capabilities
### Search & Retrieve
- Ask questions about any record, company, or contact in plain language
- Run semantic search across notes, emails, and call recordings
- Pull a full account history before a meeting without opening Attio
### Create & Update
- Update deal stages, values, and next steps as conversations happen
- Log notes against any record the moment a call ends
- Create and update tasks, assign owners, and set due dates
- Create and update records across any object in your workspace
- Build a target list and add records to it as you research.
### Meeting & Call Intelligence
- Search meetings and call recordings by metadata or meaning
- Retrieve a specific call recording or transcript
- Find the conversation where a topic came up, then read exactly what was said
- Build lists of quotes and themes across many recorded conversations
### Research & Analysis
- Surface patterns across accounts rather than one record at a time
- Assemble reports on your interactions with any company
- Extract product feedback and objections from calls at scale

snippet:
# Attio
Cursor plugin that connects agents to [Attio](https://attio.com) through Attio's official remote [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server.
Search, create, and update CRM records (people, companies, deals, and custom objects), work with lists, notes, and tasks, and search emails, meetings, and comments in the signed-in Attio workspace.
## Install
1. Open **Cursor Settings → Plugins**.
2. Search for **Attio**.
3. Click **Install**, then complete the Attio sign-in prompt.
Or run `/add-plugin attio` in chat.
## MCP
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"attio": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.attio.com/mcp"
}
}
}
```
Auth is OAuth against Attio. Cursor prompts for Attio user login when the plugin connects — there is no API key or client ID to configure.
## Before you connect
You need an Attio account with access to a workspace. Attio MCP is available to all workspace members.
## What agents can do
| Category | Capabilities |
| --- | --- |
| Records & objects | Search, create, update, upsert, and merge people, companies, deals, and custom objects |
| Lists | Inspect lists and attributes, add records, and update list entries and stages |
| Notes | Search, create, and update notes; semantic search over note content |
| Tasks | List, create, and update tasks |
| Meetings & calls | Search call recordings and transcripts |
| Emails | Search and read emails |
| Comments | List and add comments on records and list entries |
| Workspace | List members and teams; inspect the signed-in user |
| Reporting | Run basic reports; optional read-only SQL on some plans |

- Tool calls run as the Attio user who authorizes the connection and cannot exceed that user's permissions.
- Read operations are auto-approved. Write operations request confirmation before they change workspace data.
- `query-particle-sql` (read-only SQL) is not available on every Attio billing plan.
- Attio hosts the server itself; this plugin does not wrap a local stdio server.
- Revoke access at any time from your Attio account settings.

title: attio.com/help/reference/how-to-guides/attio-mcp-prompts-and-best-practices
snippet:
Attio MCP connects external AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT to your Attio workspace, so you can search your CRM, update records, log notes, and manage tasks in natural language from wherever you already work with AI.

**MCP** (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI assistants securely interact with other systems. Your AI assistant connects to Attio's MCP server, you sign in with your Attio account, and the assistant can then use a set of Attio tools: searching records, creating and updating records, working with notes and tasks, managing views, and reading emails and meeting data.
See the [full list of the Attio MCP’s tools](https://docs.attio.com/mcp/overview#supported-tools).
Three things are worth understanding before you connect:
- **It acts as you.** The AI assistant authenticates as your Attio user through OAuth. It can only see and change what your own permissions allow.
- **You control what runs without asking.** By default, your AI assistant asks for your approval before running most Attio tools. In your assistant's settings, you can allow specific tools, like read tools that search and view data, to run without asking. If you're in a managed workspace on your AI assistant, the available options may be restricted, e.g. write tools can’t be set to **Always allow**.
- **It works alongside Ask Attio, not instead of it.** Ask Attio is AI inside Attio and needs no setup. MCP is for working outside Attio, where you can combine your CRM with other tools and data the assistant can reach. Learn more about [when to use Attio MCP or Ask Attio](https://attio.com/help/reference/attio-ai/attio-mcp#when-to-use-attio-mcp-or-ask-attio).
## Before you start
- You need an Attio account on any plan. All workspace members can use the MCP.
- You need an AI assistant that supports MCP connections, such as Claude or ChatGPT. Whether connectors are available can depend on your plan with that assistant, and if your AI assistant is managed by an admin, you may need them to enable the Attio connector.
- Know which workspace you want to connect. If you belong to more than one Attio workspace, you choose one during sign-in.

Claude and ChatGPT connect through their built-in connector directories, and any other MCP-compatible assistant connects using the server URL `https://mcp.attio.com/mcp`.
